transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-04 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jordan - Arcadia (PM), Priya - Arcadia (SRE), Marcus - Arcadia (DS)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/pilot-playbook (deck), s3://redwood-bench/pilot-scripts (bench scripts)

Summary (auto): Quick weekly POC sync focusing on environment readiness and access handoff. Agreed next steps around VPC peering, SFTP credentials, and a performance run schedule. Some network firewall clarifications outstanding.

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're at the weekly pilot sync. I think we've got about 45 minutes. Quick round robin—who's on from Arcadia?
[00:08] Jordan - Arcadia (PM): Hey, Jordan here. Got Priya and Marcus on as well. We're hoping to close the env gate this week so Samir can run the bench.
[00:15] Priya - Arcadia (SRE): Yep, Priya. We did a first pass on network but have questions on the exact SG rules and whether we need NAT for the model nodes.
[00:22] Marcus - Arcadia (DS): Marcus chiming in. I have a couple of dataset access questions and also want to validate the inference perf targets.
[00:28] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi everyone, hi Jordan, Priya. I'll be doing the bench runs. Main goals today: confirm access, verify VPC peering, and baseline perf.
[00:36] Ava (Redwood AE): Cool. Quick status from our side: we pushed updated bench scripts to s3 and revised the access checklist — link in chat. We also updated the playbook to include SFTP fallback for artifact exchange.
[00:48] Jordan: Thanks. Priya, do you want to lay out what you validated so far on your end?
[00:52] Priya: Sure. We created the peering request, the route tables are updated, and we've opened 443 to the Redwood Egress IPs per the doc. The thing we're not sure on is outbound ephemeral ports; do you require a broad range for the control plane? The doc mentioned 1024-65535 but that seems wide.
[01:11] Samir: Yeah, so the control plane agent does initiate a couple of ephemeral connections for live telemetry and KV cache sync. Practically we've seen folks only need 1024-61000, but if you prefer we'll do a quick test that restricts to 1024-32768. It depends on batching levels.
[01:29] Priya: Ok that helps. Another question — KMS key usage. Do you support customer-managed KMS for model artifact encryption in the private deployment?
[01:37] Ava: Yes, for Private we support BYOK via KMS/HSM. For this pilot in dedicated mode we're offering Redwood-managed keys but we can swap to CMK if you need. There are a couple of extra steps in the playbook — we'll add them to the checklist.
[01:51] Jordan: Our compliance team prefers BYOK but for the pilot they said Redwood-managed is fine as long as we document the path to CMK.
[01:58] Marcus: On dataset access — we're planning to mount a filtered S3 bucket to the cluster. Do your bench scripts handle role chaining and STS? I remember some agents had trouble with token refresh when sessions are long.
[02:12] Samir: Good call. Our latest bench harness uses short-lived STS tokens and auto-refresh; we added a retry wrapper for the S3 getObject calls. There was one edge case where refresh jitter caused a 401 cascade — fixed in v1.2.1 of the script.
[02:26] Priya: Great. Can you confirm how the KV cache is persisted? We want to make sure nothing lingers on disk after nodes recycle.
[02:33] Samir: By default KV cache is in-memory only, but for long-lived sessions we do a transient on-disk checkpointing to /var/tmp/redwood-kv — that path can be tmpfs and wiped on reboot. We'll provide the config to disable disk checkpointing.
[02:50] Jordan: Perfect. I want to walk through the gate criteria quickly — goal is to have: 1) network validated, 2) credentials provisioned, 3) S3 access and bench scripts run locally by customer, 4) Redwood runs a baseline perf pass. If those are green we flip staging traffic.
[03:06] Ava: Sounds good. Priya, Marcus, do those criteria match your acceptance?
[03:10] Priya: Yes, with a caveat on the firewall ports.
[03:13] Marcus: Agree. Also we want latency p95 under 200ms for our 256-token default prompt; cost target TBD but we want to watch token throughput.
[03:23] Samir: For a 256-token prompt p95 sub-200 is tight but achievable on the dedicated pool with batching tuned — we'll run an initial baseline with conservative batching and then try smaller latency-optimized configs.
[03:38] Jordan: What about model variants? We're testing the 7B quantized variant initially but might move to 13B if quality regressions appear. Any caveats?
[03:46] Samir: 7B quantized is lighter on memory and gives lower latency; 13B will raise latency and memory footprints and may need a different kernel selection. We'll include both in the perf matrix.
[03:58] Ava: Let's surface the bench plan: Samir, you said you'll run a Redwood baseline from your side once the peering is validated. Marcus will run customer-local bench to make sure the S3/credentials flow. We'll compare logs.
[04:10] Samir: Right. Proposed bench: 100 users/clients ramp to 500 over 10 minutes, each session sending ~3 requests with 256 tokens response. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail GPU utilization, and context-switch latencies.
[04:27] Marcus: Sounds good. Can we also capture cold-start for KV cache? Some of our flows are bursty.
[04:33] Samir: Yep — we have a cold-start tag in the scripts.
[04:36] Priya: On access provisioning — we need the SFTP credentials as a fallback. Is that your recommended flow if peering fails?
[04:44] Ava: SFTP is a fallback for artifacts and model tarballs; it's slower for iterative benches but ok for initial artifact sync. Primary flow is VPC peering + S3 role chaining.
[04:54] Jordan: Quick procurement/legal question — Marcus flagged that our procurement requires a minimal DPIA for the dataset access. Do you have a sample DPIA or security addendum for pilot?
[05:03] Ava: We have a pilot security checklist and a short security addendum template. I'll attach them after the call. It's not a full DPIA but should satisfy the legal folks for the pilot.
[05:13] Priya: Great. Another small item — do you support IP allowlisting by service tag? Arcadia prefers to pin to a small set of egress IPs instead of CIDR ranges.
[05:23] Samir: We publish a static egress IP list for dedicated pools. We'll send that list to you. Note that in burst mode there are additional ranges; we'll call them out.
[05:33] Jordan: Excellent. Let's talk timelines — Priya, how soon can you confirm peering?
[05:38] Priya: We have infra change window Friday. If the peering request is accepted in the next 24 hours we can do a smoke test Friday afternoon.
[05:46] Ava: We can accelerate our side. I'll send the final peering CIDR and the anchor keys today. Samir, what's your earliest for the Redwood-driven baseline run?
[05:54] Samir: If peering passes on Friday I can run a baseline Friday evening Pacific. Otherwise Monday morning. I do need credentials to pull the model artifacts or SFTP fallback.
[06:05] Marcus: On model artifacts — do you provide checksums and provenance? We need to ensure model hash matches what we attest.
[06:12] Samir: Yes SHA256 checksums for artifacts and an attest file. We'll include model card metadata.
[06:18] Jordan: Great. I want to call out a small change request — can Redwood include request-level logs with a request_id header so we can tie traces back to our app logs? That helps debugging.
[06:27] Samir: We already inject an x-request-id header pass-through; we can also add an end-to-end trace id linking to the span in our console. We'll add that into the bench logging.
[06:38] Priya: Ok, for the final acceptance we also want a list of redwood console users and roles so we can map to Arcadia SSO groups.
[06:46] Ava: We'll add a CSV export of recommended RBAC mappings and the SSO SAML metadata.
[06:52] Jordan: Any concerns about data retention? Our policies want logs limited to 30 days by default during pilot, longer only on request.
[06:59] Samir: Default retention for pilot logs is 30 days; we can tweak that. Audit logs are retained longer but we can scope them.
[07:07] Marcus: I wanted to surface a perf anomaly we saw in the earlier run — some tail latency spikes correlated with GC on the JVM side of a helper service. Not sure if Redwood's runtime and our helper stack interacted.
[07:19] Samir: Interesting. Are those helper services co-located on the same subnet? If network egress was fighting for bandwidth it could cause spikes. We can instrument packet drops and queue depths in the bench.
[07:29] Marcus: We'll share the GC traces.
[07:31] Ava: Let's capture that as an action item for Marcus.

Action items (verbalized):
[07:36] Ava: Marcus — share GC traces and recent bench logs by EOD Thursday.
[07:40] Marcus: Will do.
[07:42] Ava: Priya — confirm peering and firewall rules post change window 2025-08-08.
[07:47] Priya: Yep.
[07:49] Ava: Samir — run Redwood baseline once peering validated and send raw logs 2025-08-12.
[07:55] Samir: Yep.

[08:00] Jordan: Quick question — are there any gotchas if we switch to 13B mid-pilot? Does a model swap require redeploys or can you hot-swap?
[08:09] Samir: We support hot-rollback and hot-swap to compatible model variants within the same family; a swap to a bigger architecture may require re-allocation of GPU resources but we can do a rolling swap with canary.
[08:21] Priya: And rollbacks? If the 13B introduces errors can we auto-fallback to 7B?
[08:26] Samir: Yes automatic fallback policy is available; we can configure error thresholds and latency SLOs to trigger fallback.
[08:35] Jordan: Ok good. Anything else on readiness?
[08:38] Priya: One more: local bench runs — do we have a recommended req-per-second per client figure?
[08:44] Samir: For the local harness we recommend 2-5 rps per client thread to simulate real sessions; the scripts default to 3 rps. We'll include a tuning matrix in the playbook.
[08:55] Marcus: Also, do we have a way to mask PII in logs during the pilot? Some of our test prompts contain patient-like data.
[09:03] Ava: Good catch. We have a PII masking toggle that scrubs payloads in transit for bench runs. It redacts named entities and hashes identifiers. We'll enable it by default for your project.
[09:14] Priya: Nice.

[09:16] Jordan: Let's recap next steps and owners.
[09:18] Ava: I'll send the final access checklist, SFTP creds, and security addendum by Wednesday 2025-08-06.
[09:25] Priya: We'll confirm peering after the Friday change window; target 2025-08-08 confirm.
[09:31] Samir: I'll plan the baseline run once peering is confirmed — aim for Monday 2025-08-11 if Friday doesn't work.
[09:39] Marcus: I'll push GC traces and bench logs to the shared workspace by Thursday EOD.
[09:45] Ava: Great. Any blockers?
[09:47] Jordan: Not today. This is good.
[09:49] Priya: Nope, thanks everyone.
[09:51] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with the bench report and the egress IP list.
[09:56] Ava: Okay closing — we'll send notes and action items. Thanks all.
[10:00] End of recording
